newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Media says loss narrowed in latest quarter.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Media says loss narrowed in latest quarter.

text.p: U.S. West Media Group reported Tuesday a smaller-than-expected loss for the first quarter, and said a jump in its cash flow helped the cable operator to expand its Internet access service.

The company said it lost $109 million, or 20 cents a share, as it absorbed the $11.8 billion acquisition of Continental Cablevision last year. The results compared with a slightly larger loss a year-ago of $111 million, or 20 cents a share, which was adjusted to include Continental's operations.
U.S. West said revenues rose to $2.1 billion from $1.9 billion, and operating cash flow rose 16 percent to $620 million.

The company said it expected to generate enough cash to meet aggressive goals of upgrading its cable network to provide high-speed Internet access and expanded channel service to 1 million homes by the end of the year.
The company's Highway 1 high-speed Internet access service currently reached 3,500 homes in Jacksonville, Fla., Boston and Detroit.
U.S. West said it has the broadband cable network in place to reach more than 300,000 homes, and plans to triple that by the end of the year.

New markets it plans to enter in 1997 include Los Angeles, Atlanta, Chicago, Richmond, Va., and south Florida. The company plans to eventually deliver cable television, telephone and Internet access services over a single cable.
U.S. West's stock was up 62.5 cents at $17 on the New York Stock Exchange.
